title: Safe Calculator
brief: Real programs don't crash when something goes wrong, they handle it! Your Safe Calculator divides two numbers, but wraps the risky part in try/except so a bad input (like dividing by zero, or typing a word) shows a friendly message instead of an ugly error. Finish the two lines, then press Check Project!
steps: The try block already asks for two numbers with int(input(...)).
Inside try, print the division result, like: print("Answer:", a / b).
Inside except, print a friendly message so the program never crashes.
Run it and try normal numbers, then try dividing by 0 to see except catch it.
Press Check Project to test all the cases.
starterCode:
# 🛟 Safe Calculator, it divides two numbers without ever crashing!

try:
    a = int(input("First number: "))
    b = int(input("Second number: "))
    # 1) Divide a by b and print it, like:  Answer: 5.0
    # print("Answer:", a / b)
except:
    # 2) If anything goes wrong, print a friendly message instead of crashing:
    # print("Oops! Please use numbers, and don't divide by zero.")
    pass
inputHint: Type two numbers, one on each line.

tests.name: A word instead of a number is caught

successMessage: Rock solid! 🛟 Your calculator handles divide-by-zero and bad input without ever crashing. That's exactly what try and except are for, keeping your programs friendly and safe!
